title: add-transactional-downgrade-guard-backup-restore-version-pinning-private-installer
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) need robust upgrade and rollback tooling to safely handle customer upgrades across multiple major versions. This PR implements transactional schema migration guards, explicit version pinning for installer artifacts, and an automated backup/restore flow to enable safe rollbacks and protect user data.

Summary of changes: - Add transactional migration framework to the private-installer that enforces forward-only migrations unless explicit downgrade path exists. - Introduce a downgrade guard check that blocks installer upgrades when a downgrading path is detected without a verified restore plan. - Wire up automatic logical backups (Postgres dump + object store snapshot) as part of the upgrade plan; provide an idempotent restore procedure. - Add version pinning configuration for chart, terraform modules, and runtime images to reduce accidental drift during cross-version upgrades. - Expose new CLI flags and API hooks for orchestration (--verify-backup, --force-apply-migrations, --dry-run).

Checklist: [x] transactional migration runner and rollback markers implemented; [x] backup/create/restore end-to-end flow with retries and verification; [x] helm values schema extended for version pinning; [x] terraform module refactor to accept pinned provider/module versions; [x] integration tests for upgrade/rollback happy path and restore failure modes; [x] migration docs and operator playbook added.

Testing and validation: Ran full integration tests in staging: cluster-up -> v1.18 installer -> populate data -> upgrade to v1.20 (migrations applied) -> simulated failure -> restore from backup -> confirmed data integrity. Unit tests for migration idempotency and rollback marker semantics included. CI history: initial CI run failed due to flaky restore timeout in staging which was addressed by increasing retry/backoff and adding an exponential backoff for object-store snapshots; subsequent CI passed.

Backward compatibility and rollbacks: Default behavior remains conservative: upgrades will not proceed if the downgrade guard detects non-reversible migrations unless the operator opts in with --force-apply-migrations and an explicit verified backup is present. The restore procedure is designed to be safe for common failure modes; operators are provided a recovery checklist in the release notes.

Notes for maintainers: - Keep the migration runner small and deterministic; avoid network calls during migration step besides KV reads. - Version pinning keys are intentionally namespaced under installer.versionPins to allow future overrides. - We added metrics: installer.upgrade.backup.duration, installer.upgrade.restore.success, installer.migration.applied.count.

Related work: linear/ENG-3421 and ENG-3489, incident SUP-1123 (customer outage due to failed downgrade).

release_notes: Operators: introduces transactional schema migrations with downgrade guard. Installer now performs automatic logical backups before applying migrations; a restore flow is available if migrations fail. Version pinning for helm/terraform/runtime images added to reduce drift. Default behavior blocks upgrades that are not reversible; use --force-apply-migrations with a verified backup to proceed. See docs/operator/upgrade-rollbacks.md for the recovery playbook and migration guidelines.
additional_notes: This PR was prioritized after SUP-1123. Post-merge action: coordinate a migration-runner rollout (canary 10% -> full) and notify SRE before first customer upgrade using these flows.
